input: File my health insurance reimbursement claims

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many claims and what types of expenses are involved determines the volume of work and whether different forms or processes apply to each.
The insurer and specific plan dictate the exact submission process — online portal, paper form, mobile app, or third-party processor — which completely changes the steps.
Understanding what documents the user already has (receipts, EOBs, doctor bills) vs. what still needs to be gathered determines the immediate next action.
Health insurance claims often have strict filing deadlines; knowing whether any claims are at risk of expiring changes prioritisation.
Claims could be for the user alone or for dependents (spouse, children), which may require additional authorization forms or separate submissions.
The user may prefer to handle this entirely themselves, use a reimbursement app, or want help drafting appeal letters if a prior claim was denied — this shapes the plan's approach.
Success could mean simply submitting the claims, or it could mean tracking them through to payment confirmation — knowing the end goal sets the right stopping point.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to submit one or more health insurance reimbursement claims to get paid back for medical expenses they have already incurred.

questions.title: Which expenses are you claiming — how many and what type?
questions.description: Identify the number of claims and the nature of expenses (e.g., prescriptions, hospital visits, therapy, dental) to gauge scope and whether different processes apply.

questions.title: Which insurance provider and plan are you filing with?
questions.description: The insurer and plan determine the exact submission channel and required forms — online portal, paper form, app, or third-party processor.

questions.title: Which documents do you already have ready to submit?
questions.description: Determine what the user has on hand (itemised receipts, doctor invoices, EOBs, referral letters) versus what still needs to be collected before filing.

questions.title: Are any of these claims approaching a filing deadline?
questions.description: Health insurers impose time limits on claims; knowing urgency allows the plan to prioritise time-sensitive submissions first.

questions.title: Are the claims for yourself only, or also for dependents?
questions.description: Claims for a spouse or children may require separate forms, additional authorization, or different policyholder details.

questions.title: Do you prefer to file online, by app, or on paper?
questions.description: The user's preferred submission method shapes every step in the plan and determines which tools or resources to include.

questions.title: Is your goal to submit, or to track claims through to payment?
questions.description: Clarifies where the task ends — just getting claims submitted, or following up until reimbursement is confirmed and received.
